Answer Part 1: Git Use with Engineering Workflow 10 Points

Engineering Process & Non-Self-Merge Rule: Every sprint feature was planned as an independent GitHub Issue (Issues #72–#83) on the Kanban Project Board, developed on an isolated feature/* branch, verified with local test suites, pushed to GitHub, and submitted as a formal Pull Request to lab4-staging. Under the strict course governance constraint ("ห้าม merge เองเด็ดขาด"), zero PRs were self-merged. Every PR underwent mandatory peer review by collaborator Pilaiwan Churdchu (@Pilaiwan3492), who reviewed code, tested edge cases, requested changes where necessary, approved, and merged each PR.

Answer Part 2: Spec DD 5 Points

Specification-Driven Development (SpecDD): The engineering contract was formally specified, reviewed, and merged in PR #84 (Issue #72 / LAB4-01) prior to implementing code PRs. All downstream models, APIs, UI workflows, and test assertions strictly conform to these numbered contracts:

  • 15 Functional Requirements (FR-01..15): Operational dashboards, Actions Taken lifecycle, Resolution Gate, audit logging, and role-based permissions (docs/lab-04/specification.md).
  • 17 Business Rules (BR-01..17): State machine rules (15 allowed transitions, 4 terminal blocks), resolution eligibility (>= 1 completed action or mandatory resolution note), optimistic concurrency (409 STALE_UPDATE), and deduplication (Idempotency-Key).
  • 23 Acceptance Criteria (AC-01..23): Authoritative operational metric calculations, role isolation, multi-viewport responsive guarantees, and visual accessibility standards.
  • Database & Migration Decisions: Added ActionTaken and IdempotencyRecord models in PostgreSQL; pure idempotent SQL migrations; dynamic synchronization of ticket_number_seq in seed.
EVD-REL-04: Sprint 4 Engineering Contract Package Audit (specification.md, api-spec.md, ui-spec.md, tests.md) showing 100% bidirectional traceability.

Answer Part 4: AI Use with Reflection 5 Points

EVD-REL-07: AI Use Record & Methodology Reflection (docs/lab-04/ai-use.md).
My Reflection: Specification-Agent vs. Coding-Agent Workflow

In Lab 4, utilizing Google Antigravity Agentic IDE powered by Gemini 2.0 (Coding & Planning Agent) and Gemini 1.5 Pro (Specification & Architectural Agent) reinforced the necessity of strict workflow separation between specification and execution:

1. Specification-First Prevents Rework: Treating the Specification Agent as a formal systems architect produced unambiguous contracts (FR-01..15, BR-01..17, AC-01..23). In Sprint 4, explicitly defining the 15 valid status transitions and 4 terminal blocks upfront eliminated race conditions and conflicting UI states during implementation.

2. Coding Agent as Rigorous Pair Programmer: The Coding Agent implemented atomic Prisma database transactions, optimistic concurrency protection (409 STALE_UPDATE), and header-based idempotency. Peer review feedback from collaborator Pilaiwan Churdchu identified subtle issues (e.g. database updatedAt mutation during cleanup and missing Ticket state assertions in ACT-07), which the Coding Agent resolved by introducing dynamic snapshotting and raw SQL restoration in test cleanup.

3. Traceability & Continuous Auditing: Automated cross-document audit scripts ensured zero drift between specification.md, api-spec.md, ui-spec.md, and tests.md, proving that AI assistance is most potent when bound to machine-verifiable engineering gates.
